generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1; unique; never NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy an existing parent key value from the parent's reserved non-orphan pool; allow NULL only if column is nullable; each instance must include at least one NULL (if nullable) and at least one parent row with no child rows. The reserved unreferenced parent key must be chosen from parent keys that are NOT referenced by any compact child row and NOT referenced by any generated child row; reserve one such key per FK relationship and exclude it from the FK draw pool.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_numeric: Uniform integer within the column's range rule; guarantee each listed boundary literal and one step on each side appears at least once per instance (deterministic injection, not probabilistic). Values drawn from the boundary literal pool are injected verbatim and are never perturbed by arithmetic steps; only free uniform draws may be perturbed.
generic_sampling_rules.real_numeric: Uniform real within the column's range rule, rounded to 2 decimals; guarantee each listed boundary literal and one step on each side appears at least once per instance (deterministic injection). Boundary literals are injected verbatim and never perturbed.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Pick from a small pool of distinct values; allow near-duplicates (case/whitespace variants) and NULL if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Pick uniformly from the enumerated value list; NULL if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_date: Format 'Month D' (e.g. 'December 2'); generate dates from an expanding fresh generator that yields N distinct date strings for N rows (fresh_value_share of the pool is newly minted per instance, not drawn from a fixed 21-element pool); NULL if nullable. Composite PK (Exhibition_ID, Date) uniqueness is enforced per Exhibition_ID group: after FK assignment, for each Exhibition_ID group the Date values must be distinct; dedupe (Exhibition_ID, Date) tuples and regenerate colliding dates until the full tuple set is unique.

targets.note: Negative literals are unreachable because Ticket_Price >= 0; only non-negative boundary literals are sampled.

targets.per_group_avg: Computed over the FULL merged instance (compact + generated rows). For at least one Exhibition_ID group the group average Attendance must be < 200, and for at least one (possibly different) group the average must be > 200; across instances the exact value 200 must also occur as a group average. The generator must choose Exhibition_IDs for the low/high/exact groups that are not contaminated by compact rows (i.e. groups composed only of generated rows, or groups whose compact rows are adjusted/absent), and must verify the target on the merged data after composite-PK dedup and before writing. Execution feedback must report per-group AVG straddling 200 (both sides 199/201 and exact 200).

dependencies.rule: UNIQUE(Exhibition_ID, Date) enforced per Exhibition_ID group after FK assignment; dedupe tuples and regenerate colliding dates; assert zero rows skipped by the writer for exhibition_record.

generation_specification.uncertainty: No calculated columns or date-order pairs exist. Nullable columns have 0% NULL in the sample but are declared nullable, so NULLs are generated per the NULL rule: at least one NULL per nullable column per instance, with share floor 0.15 (not a tracked compact share). Ticket_Price negative boundary literals (-5.01, -5, -4.99) are unreachable under Ticket_Price >= 0 and are excluded from sampling. Composite PK (Exhibition_ID, Date) uniqueness is enforced per Exhibition_ID group after FK assignment; the writer must report zero skipped rows for exhibition_record and the generator must assert on the actual (Exhibition_ID, Date) tuple set before writing. Boundary literals are injected verbatim and never perturbed by arithmetic steps; only free uniform draws may be perturbed. Per-group AVG(Attendance) straddling 200 is computed over the full merged instance (compact + generated rows) and must be verified by execution feedback; groups used for the low/high/exact targets must not be contaminated by compact rows. Parent-rows-without-children is enforced deterministically by reserving one parent key per FK relationship that is not referenced by any compact or generated child row, and excluding it from the child FK draw pool; a post-write check must confirm at least one parent row has no child rows for each FK relationship. After fixing the composite-PK skip, re-verify that Attendance NULL share meets the 0.15 floor on the written rows.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_build_table` fills FK columns by `rng.choice(pv)` over parent rows, then applies `apply_null_rule` to every nullable non-PK column including FK columns. The spec's `integer_fk` rule requires 'at least one NULL and at least one parent row without children' and the atomic ops for exhibition.Artist_ID / exhibition_record.Exhibition_ID require `parent_rows_without_children: true`. Execution feedback shows exhibition.Artist_ID NULL 20/105 and exhibition_record.Exhibition_ID NULL 0/154 (the latter is NOT NULL per schema, fine), but there is no evidence that any parent row is left without children. With 6 exhibitions and 13 exhibition_record rows drawn uniformly, every exhibition is almost certainly referenced; likewise every artist is referenced by some exhibition. The 'parent_rows_without_children' target is not enforced anywhere in the code.
issues.requested_revision: Add explicit construction logic (in instance.py) that guarantees at least one parent row in `artist` and `exhibition` has no child rows in the generated instance (e.g. reserve one parent key and exclude it from the FK draw pool), and verify via execution feedback that `parent_rows_without_children` holds for both FK relationships.

issues.evidence: Spec `integer_fk` says 'allow NULL only if column is nullable; include at least one NULL and at least one parent row without children.' The atomic ops for exhibition.Artist_ID and artist.Artist_ID both list `child_rows_with_null_fk: true`. Execution feedback shows exhibition.Artist_ID NULL 20/105 (OK), but the FK draw in `_build_table` uses `rng.choice(pv)` where `pv` is the parent key list; if `pv` is empty it sets all NULL. There is no guarantee of a mix of NULL and non-NULL per instance beyond the probabilistic null rule; with 6 rows and 15% null share, some instances may have zero NULL FK rows. The spec requires 'at least one NULL' per nullable column per instance, which `apply_null_rule` does enforce (k=max(1,...)), so this is satisfied — but the 'parent_rows_without_children' half is not.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows 'exhibition_record:UNIQUE constraint failed': 42 rows skipped — these are composite PK (Exhibition_ID, Date) duplicates. instance._build_table dedups via sample_fresh_primary_keys(tm, cols) on the composite PK, but the Date column is populated from a fixed DATE_POOL of only 21 strings. The spec's stated fix ('enforcing composite PK (Exhibition_ID, Date) uniqueness after FK assignment') is insufficient with a 21-element pool. issues.evidence: The literal_pool seeded from query SQLs (pool_values=122) is routed by seed_literal_pool_from_queries, and _init_sampler adds sorted({str(v) for v in literal_pool}) to the number sampler's `elements`. But in NumberSampler.sample, when a value is drawn from elements it is then randomly +/- stepped ('if r.random() < 1/6: v += d ...'). This mutates boundary literals like 199,200,201 into 198,201,202 etc., so the exact boundary literal itself is not guaranteed to appear. _inject_boundaries overwrites positions afterwards, but with pool entries competing for the same positions via rng.sample(...) and rng.shuffle(...), and with the total number of injected positions = len(planted) ≤ n, many boundary values that were overwritten lose their guarantee only if positions are fewer than planted. With n=13/6/7 this is generally OK, but the sampler itself also corrupts pool entries so OTHER non-boundary targets (e.g. Attendance literals other than the 9 specified boundaries from the query pool) may be replaced. This is minor, but the specification does not authorize arithmetic perturbation of injected boundary values.
issues.requested_revision: Either (a) remove the +-= step perturbation for values that came from the boundary literal pool (keep it only for random uniform draws), or (b) state explicitly in the specification that 'boundary literals are guaranteed at least once by injection'' and that pool-derived values may be perturbed; then lower bounds in the checker account for the small n.

issues.evidence: Specification declares NULL targets for all nullable columns and a NULL share 'following the compact database's share; NULL_FLOOR = 0.15'. Execution feedback shows 'artist.Age: generated rows: NULL 20 / 146' etc. which is 0.137, close to floor. However the multiplicity — every nullable column has exactly 20 NULLs across 20 instances = exactly 1 planted NULL per instance per nullable column — is not the natural 'follow compact share' result: it is exactly the 'at least one planted NULL' floor. So the spec's 'following the compact share' claim is not actually implemented, only the floor. Likewise the FK column exhibition.Artist_ID has NULL 20 / 118 (exactly 1 per instance), regardless of having a mixed pool; the FK-specific mix (one NULL + one non-NULL) was implemented, but non-FK columns use apply_null_rule with share=max(compact_share, 0.15); since compact shares are ~0, this yields exactly 1 null per instance per column across 20 instances because n=7/6/13 per instance * 0.15 = 1–2. So the behavior is defensible but the spec should note the deterministic floor and the presentation is misleading. Not a blocking error, but a documentation/spec discrepancy.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: rows_skipped = {"exhibition_record": 20} with diag {"exhibition_record:UNIQUE constraint failed": 20}. issues.evidence: Spec: 'integer_fk: ... each instance must include at least one NULL (if nullable) and at least one parent row with no child rows (reserve one parent key and exclude it from the FK draw pool).' The program's _reserve_unreferenced_parents reserves one key per FK relationship, but _build_table draws FK values from parent_rows which includes generated parent rows appended during the same instance build. For exhibition.Artist_ID, parent_rows['artist'] is extended with generated artist IDs, and the reserved key is chosen from compact_vals only. If the reserved key is a compact artist ID, generated exhibition rows could still reference it only if it appears in pv — it is filtered out, so that part is fine. However, the reservation is per (parent_table, parent_col) and only one key is reserved; with 6 exhibition rows and 7 artist rows, the 'parent row with no child' requirement is satisfied only if the reserved artist is not referenced by any compact exhibition row either. The compact exhibition rows may already reference the reserved artist, so the 'parent row without children' target is not guaranteed. No execution evidence confirms a parent row with zero children.

issues.evidence: Spec: 'text_date: ... generate dates from an expanding fresh generator that yields N distinct date strings for N rows (fresh_value_share of the pool is newly minted per instance, not drawn from a fixed 21-element pool)'. The program's _fresh_dates draws n_pool values from DATE_POOL with `pool[i % len(pool)]` after shuffling, which can repeat if n_pool > len(pool) (13 rows, 21 pool entries, so no repeat here), but the fresh minting uses `used = set(out) | set(DATE_POOL)` and skips any date already in DATE_POOL — so fresh dates are distinct from pool dates and from each other. This part is consistent. However, the spec's fresh_value_share is 0.3 and the program uses max(1, round(0.3*n)) = 4 fresh for n=13, which is fine. The real problem is the composite PK collision (issue 1), not the date generator itself.

issues.evidence: The specification requires boundary literals injected verbatim and never perturbed. NumberSampler.sample() checks _boundary_set and sets from_boundary=True when a drawn element equals a boundary, skipping perturbation. _inject_boundaries plants boundaries verbatim. However, _inject_boundaries may overwrite a planted boundary with a later planted value if positions collide (rng.sample ensures distinct positions when n >= len(planted), so no collision). When n < len(planted), positions = [i % n for i in range(len(planted))] can repeat, causing later planted values to overwrite earlier ones — potentially dropping a required boundary literal. With table sizes 7/6/13 and Attendance having 9 boundaries (plus steps = up to 27 planted values), n=13 < 27, so some boundaries may be overwritten.
issues.requested_revision: In _inject_boundaries, when n < len(planted), ensure each distinct boundary literal (not each step) appears at least once by prioritizing the boundary values over the ±step values, or deduplicate planted values and cap to n distinct values. This affects the guarantee that every listed boundary literal appears at least once per instance for exhibition_record.Attendance (9 boundaries vs 13 rows).
